boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all four frozen records in Longstreet's Tidewater Operations [March-April 1863]. Preserve per-engagement dates: Fort Anderson March 13–15, Washington March 30–April 20, Suffolk (Norfleet House) April 13–15 and Suffolk (Fort Huger/Hill's Point) April 11–May 4, 1863. VA030's frozen interval lies inside VA031's, and both frozen casualty texts refer to one 1,160 siege total; their quantities must not be added. The live NPS campaign dates do not replace any battle interval. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the 1st Division, XVIII Corps and Hill's Division without counts; the live field reads zero. NPS says Longstreet directed Hill to advance on New Berne with about 12,000 men. Foster reports the enemy's whole force, from deserters, as 13,000 infantry and cavalry with thirty-nine guns, and in his longer report of the same date as about 13,000 to 14,000; he says Pettigrew attacked the work with 7,000 men and seventeen guns. Hill says the Deep Gully position was defended by five companies and two guns. No Union count for the engagement is given.
claims.rationale: Expedition, deserter-reported and detachment figures differ in scope and source; none is adopted as matched opening strength. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: NPS says Longstreet directed Hill to advance on New Berne. Hill says he went with Daniel's brigade on the lower Trent road, sent Robertson to cut the railroad, and that Pettigrew was to bombard the shipping and barracks from the other side. Foster reads the plan as Pettigrew taking the work so that rifled batteries could drive off the gunboats and shell the town, and supposes the attack was timed for the anniversary of the town's capture.
claims.rationale: Hill's plan is his own report; Foster's reading and supposition are an opponent's inference. No inspected orders.

claims.value: NPS says Whiting refused to cooperate. Hill says Daniel in person carried Deep Gully, that Robertson did not go himself and Garnett did not start until Sunday, and that Whiting's spirit spoiled everything. Foster says Lieutenant-Colonel Anderson declined several demands to surrender and that he instructed him to hold the work. The live heading ranks Hill Colonel against the frozen Major General.
claims.rationale: Command friction and orders from two interested reports and a summary; the Deep Gully and Fort Anderson actions had different local commanders, and the frozen commanders Anderson and Hill do not receive automatic sole credit. The heading rank is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. NPS says Hill was forced to retire when Union gunboats arrived; Foster says the gunboats and a rifled battery compelled Pettigrew to withdraw, and that the enemy retired on the morning of the 15th. Hill calls the expedition partly successful.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Hill's phrase characterizes the expedition, not the frozen engagement result.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 7 total; the live NPS field reads zero. Foster reports his loss as only 2 killed and 4 wounded; the compiler's footnote gives the 92nd New York 3 men wounded and 3 missing, with 1 man reported killed on March 13. Hill calls the Confederate loss slight and gives no count.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The frozen 7 has no side split and its scope is not established.

open_questions: Pettigrew's, Daniel's and Robertson's reports, the navy reports and any Union return remain deferred; whether the frozen 7 covers Deep Gully is unknown.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Foster's, D. H. Hill's, Peck's and French's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XVIII, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. The compiler's footnote is counted with the Foster selection, and Longstreet's indorsement with French's report, for the effort ceiling; neither is treated as independent corroboration. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
